Agent Name: Planner  
Step Number: 4  
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a critical error in Step 4 by concluding that option C (cold temperatures) is the most supported answer based on the provided evidence. The sources cited, including the Britannica and NOAA pages, explicitly mention that onshore winds (sea breezes) often lead to localized showers and enhanced rainfall due to low-level convergence and upward movement of moist air along the sea-breeze front. While coastal cooling and marine-layer stability are also mentioned, they do not negate the likelihood of heavier rainfall in regions with prevailing onshore winds. This misinterpretation of the evidence and failure to prioritize the more relevant phenomenon (heavier rainfall) led to the incorrect conclusion that cold temperatures (option C) are more likely than heavier rainfall (option A).
